parts.gloss: having suited or being in right measure

words.gloss: is like being in the right measure

literal: Feigned anger is like salt in right measure; allowing that to prolong is like being a little excessive.
translation: Feigned anger in love is like salt in food; it is delightful in the right measure, but to prolong it is like adding a little too much.
modern: ஊடல் கொள்வது உணவில் உப்பு அளவாக இருப்பதற்கு ஒப்பானது; ஆனால் அந்த ஊடலை நீட்டிக்கச் செய்வது உப்பு சற்றே அதிகமாகிப் போவதற்கு ஒப்பானது.
explanation: This couplet uses a simple culinary analogy to explain the role of feigned anger (புலவி) in love. Just as a moderate amount of salt (உப்பு) makes food delicious, a brief period of pouting adds flavor and excitement to a relationship. However, if the lovers prolong this disagreement (நீள விடல்), it becomes like adding too much salt (மிக்கற்றால்), which ruins the entire experience. The words 'அமைந்தற்றால்' (like being in right measure) and 'மிக்கற்றால்' (like being excessive) highlight the importance of moderation in lovers' tiffs.
